title: An involutive perspective on Eisenstein's proof of quadratic reciprocity
summary: We revisit Eisenstein's geometric proof of quadratic reciprocity and make explicit the involutive symmetry underlying Eisenstein's lattice-point argument. Building on Gauss's lemma, we interpret the Legendre symbols as counts of lattice points in a finite rectangle and construct a simple fixed-point-free involution corresponding to the central symmetry of the rectangle, which exchanges points above and below the line $qx=py$.
